extracted.intended_audience: funders, journal editors, institutions, preprint review services, and researchers interested in recognition of preprint peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation for a community meeting and recommendations aiming to promote recognition of peer review conducted on preprints by funders, institutions, and journals, and to improve equity, visibility, and evaluation of preprints with reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefits of public review of preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: Public review of preprints offers many benefits: it enables reviewers to focus on the science itself, allows authors to engage in constructive dialog with reviewers, and provides context on preprints for readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use public review to prioritize scientific critique over gatekeeping, facilitate author–reviewer engagement, and supply readers with added context (e.g., review reports attached to preprints). This is presented as the rationale for promoting preprint review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of peer-reviewed preprints as publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Funders and institutions should recognize peer-reviewed preprints as peer-reviewed publications (examples: cOAlition S and EMBO Postdoctoral Fellowships announcing such recognition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy change at funder and institutional level should treat preprints that have undergone review as equivalent to traditional peer-reviewed outputs for assessment and eligibility purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of reviews from external preprint review services
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals should accept reviews produced by dedicated preprint review services (examples cited: Peer Community In and Review Commons).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage journals to accept or consider external review reports originating from community preprint review services as part of editorial/peer-review workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create policies that recognize both preprints with reviews and reviews of preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: Funder, institutional, and journal policies should explicitly recognize both (a) preprints that have reviews attached and (b) standalone reviews of preprints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy language should cover both the reviewed preprint as a citable/assessable output and the review itself as a scholarly contribution that can be counted or credited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote equity in visibility, curation, and evaluation of preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: Efforts around preprint review should aim to promote equity in how preprints are made visible, curated, and evaluated across communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies and practices should consider equitable access and recognition (who sees and curates reviews, whose reviews count in assessments), though the page does not give operational rules—this is stated as a meeting theme/goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop recommendations through multi-stakeholder working groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations and policy proposals should be developed by convening working groups representing Funders, Researchers, Institutions, Journals, and Preprint Review Services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ASAPbio convened two working groups (Journals & Preprint Review Projects; Funder, Researcher, and Institution) to produce presentations and archived recommendations (available on ASAPbio/Zenodo). The page implies stakeholder-inclusive processes are a recommended approach for policy development.
